productName: Rainbow AI — FnB Widget Bug Fixes (Image 3 + Image 4)
overview: Fix two critical bugs visible in screenshots: (1) hostel fallback text appearing in makan-moments cafe widget (UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES hardcoded hostel text), (2) raw JSON object rendered in chat bubble instead of plain text (chatWithToolsLoop returns unguarded LLM content). Also fix webchat-api not injecting FnB tools and unicode corruption in system prompt.
goals: Fix Image 3: hostel fallback text ('bookings, check-in/out, amenities') never appears in makan-moments widget
Fix Image 4: raw JSON '{"intent":...}' never rendered in chat bubble — chatWithToolsLoop sanitizes LLM output
Fix webchat-api tool injection: /chat/makan-moments widget gets FnB tool-calling capability
Fix unicode corruption in system prompt (em dash + rainbow emoji garbled)
Graceful tool-failure fallback: if FNB_MCP_URL is down, AI gives a helpful answer instead of hostel fallback
Regression tests for both image bugs

userStories.title: Fix hostel fallback text appearing in makan-moments AI waiter
userStories.description: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en in ai-response-generator.ts is hardcoded as 'I can help with bookings, check-in/out, amenities, and general hostel information.' When chatWithToolsLoop exhausts its 3 loops (e.g. FNB_MCP_URL is down), this hostel-specific text is returned to the makan-moments cafe widget (Image 3 bug). Fix by adding per-profile fallback support: read unknownFallback from the profile's settings.json so each profile can override the default, and set makan-moments to a cafe-appropriate fallback.

userStories.title: Fix raw JSON displayed in chat widget when LLM returns JSON format
userStories.description: chatWithToolsLoop returns the raw LLM content string without checking if it is JSON. When the LLM responds in the old structured format {'intent':'menu_query','action':'llm_reply','response':'...','confidence':0.0}, the entire JSON string is sent to the chat widget and rendered verbatim (Image 4 bug). Fix: add a looksLikeJson guard in chatWithToolsLoop — if content looks like JSON, try to extract the 'response' or 'text' field; if none found, use the profile fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: chatWithToolsLoop never returns a string starting with '{' to the caller
If LLM content is valid JSON with a 'response' or 'text' string field, that field value is returned
If JSON has no extractable text, profile-aware fallback is returned instead
Test: mock chatWithFallback to return '{"intent":"menu_query","response":"Test reply","confidence":0.5}' — chatWithToolsLoop must return 'Test reply'
npm run build passes
technicalNotes: Edit src/assistant/ai-response-generator.ts: in chatWithToolsLoop, at line 141 where `return content || UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en`, add guard: if (content && looksLikeJson(content)) { try { const j = JSON.parse(content); const extracted = j.response || j.text || j.message || null; if (extracted && typeof extracted === 'string' && !looksLikeJson(extracted)) return extracted; } catch {} return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en; } return content || UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en

Also apply the same guard at line 182 (max loops exhausted last content): before returning UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en, check if the last message in messages has content that looks like JSON and try to extract from it.

userStories.title: Inject FnB tools into webchat-api for makan-moments profile
userStories.description: webchat-api.ts (/api/chat/:profileId/message) calls processChat() WITHOUT tools for ALL profiles. This means the embedded rainbow-ai widget at /chat/makan-moments cannot use FnB tools (menu lookup, order placement). Fix: when profileId === 'makan-moments', pass toolRegistry.getToolsForProfile('makan-moments') and toolRegistry.getHandlersForProfile('makan-moments') to processChat().
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/chat/makan-moments/message triggers chatWithToolsLoop (tool_use intent in result)
POST /api/chat/pelangi/message still uses the non-tool path (no tools passed)
Tool injection does not break other profiles
npm run build passes
technicalNotes: Edit src/routes/public/webchat-api.ts: add import { toolRegistry } from '../../tools/registry.js'. In the POST handler, after resolving profile, before calling processChat(), add: const fnbTools = profileId === 'makan-moments' ? toolRegistry.getToolsForProfile('makan-moments') : []; const fnbHandlers = profileId === 'makan-moments' ? toolRegistry.getHandlersForProfile('makan-moments') : new Map(); Then add tools: fnbTools, toolHandlers: fnbHandlers to the processChat() call.

userStories.title: chatWithToolsLoop graceful fallback: answer without tools if all tool calls fail
userStories.description: When FNB_MCP_URL is unavailable, every tool call in chatWithToolsLoop returns an error. The LLM sees 3 rounds of error responses and finally exhausts max loops, returning an unhelpful fallback. Fix: track if ALL tool calls across loops failed. If so, make one final LLM call WITHOUT tools (just the conversation) to get at least a helpful general response, before falling back to the profile fallback text.
acceptanceCriteria: When all tool results have isError:true, chatWithToolsLoop makes a final toolless LLM call
Final call uses the same system prompt and conversation history but no tools array
If final call also fails, returns profile-aware fallback (not hardcoded hostel text)
Test: mock all tool handlers to return {isError:true} — result should be a non-empty meaningful text, not the hostel fallback
npm run build passes
technicalNotes: Edit src/assistant/ai-response-generator.ts chatWithToolsLoop: add a boolean allToolsFailed = false. After the loop, if all tool calls had isError:true (track with a counter), make one extra call: const { content: finalContent } = await chatWithFallback(messages.filter(m => m.role !== 'tool'), maxTokens, temp, false, undefined, undefined). Return finalContent if truthy and not JSON. The messages filtered are the original without tool results.

userStories.title: Profile-scoped admin tab URLs: every tab includes profileId in hash
userStories.description: The admin panel URL only encodes the tab name (e.g. #intents, #responses) but never the active profile. Switching from hostel to cafe profile only updates localStorage — the URL stays the same. This causes cross-profile data bleed: a user on #intents may see hostel intents instead of cafe intents because the API calls use a stale x-profile-id header. Fix: update all profile-specific tabs to include profileId in the URL (#intents/makan-moments, #responses/pelangi, etc.) following the pattern already used by #dashboard/makan-moments/tests. Switching profiles updates the URL; loading a URL auto-switches to the correct profile. Global tabs (settings, whatsapp, staff-review, help) keep the current flat URL.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to #intents/makan-moments auto-switches to makan-moments profile and loads cafe intents
Navigating to #intents/pelangi auto-switches to pelangi profile and loads hostel intents
When profileSwitcher.switchTo() is called, the URL updates to #currentTab/newProfileId
Tabs that are profile-specific update their URL on load if profileId is missing (redirect #intents → #intents/activeProfileId)
Global tabs (settings, whatsapp, staff-review, help, live-chat) do NOT get a profileId in the URL
Profile-specific tabs: dashboard, intents, understanding, responses, performance, chat-simulator, tests, knowledge-base, workflows
Refreshing the page restores both the tab and the profile from the URL
getTabInfoFromUrl() returns {main, profileId, sub} — profileId is parts[1] if it matches a known profile ID, else null

Sub becomes parts[2] when profileId is present.

userStories.title: WhatsApp opt-out tracking and 24-hour compliance processing enforcement
userStories.description: Meta's WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy requires that opt-out requests (STOP, unsubscribe, block) are honored within 24 hours. The current system has an opt-out endpoint but no dashboard to verify compliance or track the processing timeline. Failure to comply can result in Business Account suspension.
acceptanceCriteria: When a user sends a STOP/opt-out keyword, their phone is flagged in the database within 1 message-processing cycle
Opted-out numbers are never sent outbound WhatsApp messages (broadcast, scheduled, or escalation notification)
Admin panel shows a list of opted-out numbers with the timestamp of their opt-out request
Admin panel shows whether each opt-out was processed (messages stopped) within 24 hours
A warning banner is displayed in the admin dashboard if any opt-out took more than 24 hours to process
Opt-out status is persisted per phone number and survives server restarts
technicalNotes: Add opted_out_at and opted_out_processed_at columns to rainbow_conversations or a new opt_out_registry table
Extend intent pipeline: if incoming message matches opt-out intent, set opted_out_at and block future sends immediately
Add GET /api/admin/opt-outs?profileId= endpoint listing opted-out numbers with compliance status
All outbound send functions must check opt-out registry before calling Baileys sendMessage

userStories.title: Enforce WhatsApp 24-hour session window check before sending outbound messages
userStories.description: Meta requires that free-form outbound messages can only be sent within 24 hours of the last user-initiated message. Sending outside this window fails silently or returns an error, but the current system has no pre-send session window check. This risks silent delivery failures for scheduled messages, payment reminders, and escalation notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: All outbound WhatsApp send paths check if the 24-hour session window is active before sending
If the session is expired, the message is blocked from sending and logged with reason='session_expired'
Admin conversations list shows a 'Session Active' or 'Session Expired' status indicator per conversation
Scheduled and broadcast messages that fail the session window check are queued as pending rather than dropped silently
If a WhatsApp Message Template is configured for the profile, it is used as fallback when session is expired
Session window checks apply to all outbound paths: broadcast, scheduled, escalation notification
technicalNotes: Add sessionWindowActive(phone: string): Promise<boolean> helper in src/lib/ or src/assistant/
Implementation: query rainbow_messages WHERE role='user' AND phone=? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1, check timestamp within 24h
Wrap all Baileys sendMessage calls with a session window guard
Add session_active field to the GET /api/admin/conversations list API response

userStories.title: Sentiment-based early escalation trigger in message processing pipeline
userStories.description: Current escalation triggers are intent-based, requiring users to explicitly request help. Frustrated or angry language is not detected, meaning the bot continues attempting to handle the situation without proactive human handoff. A lightweight sentiment check before intent classification enables early escalation before frustration peaks.
acceptanceCriteria: Messages containing strong negative sentiment markers are detected in the pipeline before intent classification
If a user sends 3 or more messages with negative sentiment in a single session, the pipeline escalates to human
The escalation message to the user is empathetic and acknowledges frustration (configurable per profile)
Sentiment detection can be enabled or disabled per profile in admin settings
Sentiment-triggered escalation events are recorded in escalation_events table with reason='sentiment'
Sentiment detection does not add more than 50ms to the average message processing time
technicalNotes: Use a rule-based keyword/phrase list (not a separate LLM call) to avoid latency and cost
Initial negative marker set (EN): 'useless', 'terrible', 'awful', 'angry', 'never again', repeated '!!', 'ridiculous'
Track consecutive_negative_messages counter in session context (in-memory, not persisted to DB)
Add sentiment_escalation_enabled and sentiment_threshold to profile settings.json
Optional: include sentiment as a classified field in existing intent classification LLM prompt to avoid extra round-trip
